passages.text: Job continued his discourse: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul— as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils, my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke again.
Job continued his speech.
God lives.
God has taken away my justice.
The Almighty has made my soul bitter.
My breath is still in me.
The breath of God is in my nostrils.
My lips will not speak wickedness.
My tongue will not speak lies.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ חַי־ אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃ כִּֽי־ כָל־ ע֣וֹד נִשְׁמָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְר֖וּחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּאַפִּֽי׃ אִם־ תְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנִ֗י אִם־ יֶהְגֶּ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job’s friends accuse him of wrongdoing.
Job answers his friends.
Job says, “I will not say you are right.”
Job refuses to agree with their accusations.
Job says, “I will keep my integrity.”
Job will hold to his innocence.
Job will do this until he dies.
passages.original: חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם־ אַצְדִּ֪יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם עַד־ אֶגְוָ֑ע לֹא־ אָסִ֖יר תֻּמָּתִ֣י מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job holds on to his righteousness.
He will not let go of his righteousness.
He will keep his righteousness always.
As long as Job lives, his conscience will not accuse him.
His heart will not blame him all his days.
passages.original: בְּצִדְקָתִ֣י הֶ֭חֱזַקְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֑הָ לֹֽא־ יֶחֱרַ֥ף לְ֝בָבִ֗י מִיָּמָֽי׃

passages.text: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
passages.sermon:
My enemy opposes me.
My enemy acts against me.
I want my enemy to be like the wicked.
I want my opponent to be like the unjust.
The wicked do evil.
The unjust act wrongly.
Let my enemy and my opponent share the fate of the wicked and the unjust.

passages.text: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
passages.sermon:
The godless person rejects God.
He does not follow God’s ways.
He lives without faith in God.
God may cut off the godless person.
God can take away his life.
When God takes away his life, he has no hope.
The godless person cannot hope for anything good from God after this.
He has no lasting hope.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מַה־ תִּקְוַ֣ת חָ֭נֵף כִּ֣י יִבְצָ֑ע כִּ֤י יֵ֖שֶׁל אֱל֣וֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
passages.sermon:
God is the Almighty.
A wicked person may cry out to God.
Distress comes upon the wicked person.
Will God hear his cry?
passages.original: הַֽ֭צַעֲקָתוֹ יִשְׁמַ֥ע׀ אֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ תָב֖וֹא עָלָ֣יו צָרָֽה׃

passages.text: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
passages.sermon:
The godless man does not delight in the Almighty.
He does not find joy in God.
He does not call upon God at all times.
He does not pray to God regularly.
passages.original: אִם־ עַל־ שַׁדַּ֥י יִתְעַנָּ֑ג יִקְרָ֖א אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּכָל־ עֵֽת׃

passages.text: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.
passages.sermon: I will teach you about God's power.\r\nI will show you what the Almighty does.\r\nI will not hide the ways of the Almighty from you.
passages.original: אוֹרֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֣ם בְּיַד־ אֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־ שַׁ֝דַּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲכַחֵֽד׃

passages.text: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?
passages.sermon:
You have all seen this with your own eyes.
You know what has happened.
Why do you continue to speak empty words?
Why do you keep talking about things that are meaningless?
passages.original: הֵן־ אַתֶּ֣ם כֻּלְּכֶ֣ם חֲזִיתֶ֑ם וְלָמָּה־ זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל תֶּהְבָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man receives a portion from God.
Ruthless people receive an inheritance from the Almighty.
God gives this portion to the wicked.
The Almighty gives this heritage to the ruthless.
passages.original: זֶ֤ה׀ חֵֽלֶק־ אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע׀ עִם־ אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.
passages.sermon:
The wicked man may have many sons.
His sons will die by the sword.
His descendants will not have enough food.
God gives this fate to the wicked.
passages.original: אִם־ יִרְבּ֣וּ בָנָ֣יו לְמוֹ־ חָ֑רֶב וְ֝צֶאֱצָאָ֗יו לֹ֣א יִשְׂבְּעוּ־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.
passages.sermon: The wicked man’s survivors will die in the plague.\r\nPeople will bury them.\r\nTheir widows will not cry for them.
passages.original: שְׂרִידוֹ בַּמָּ֣וֶת יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃

passages.text: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay, what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man gathers much silver.
He gathers silver as if it were dust.
He prepares clothing as if it were clay.
He stores up wealth and garments.
But a righteous person will wear those garments.
An innocent person will divide that silver.
The wicked man does not keep what he gathers.
Others, who are righteous and innocent, will receive it.
passages.original: אִם־ יִצְבֹּ֣ר כֶּעָפָ֣ר כָּ֑סֶף וְ֝כַחֹ֗מֶר יָכִ֥ין מַלְבּֽוּשׁ׃ יָ֭כִין וְצַדִּ֣יק יִלְבָּ֑שׁ וְ֝כֶ֗סֶף נָקִ֥י יַחֲלֹֽק׃

passages.text: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man builds his house.
His house is weak.
His house is like a moth’s cocoon.
A moth’s cocoon is fragile.
His house is also like a hut.
A watchman sets up a hut for a short time.
The hut is not strong or lasting.
The wicked man’s house will not last.
passages.original: בָּנָ֣ה כָעָ֣שׁ בֵּית֑וֹ וּ֝כְסֻכָּ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה נֹצֵֽר׃

passages.text: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
passages.sermon:
A rich man lies down to sleep.
He is wealthy.
He will not rise again.
He opens his eyes.
Everything is gone.
passages.original: עָשִׁ֣יר יִ֭שְׁכַּב וְלֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑ף עֵינָ֖יו פָּקַ֣ח וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
passages.sermon:
Terrors come to him suddenly.
They come like a flood of water.
A violent storm sweeps him away.
This happens during the night.
passages.original: תַּשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ כַ֭מַּיִם בַּלָּה֑וֹת לַ֝֗יְלָה גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה׃

passages.text: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
passages.sermon:
The east wind comes.
The east wind carries the man away.
The man is gone.
The east wind sweeps the man out of his place.

passages.text: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
passages.sermon:
A great force attacks him.
This force shows no mercy.
He runs away quickly.
He tries to escape from its power.
passages.original: וְיַשְׁלֵ֣ךְ עָ֭לָיו וְלֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל מִ֝יָּד֗וֹ בָּר֥וֹחַ יִבְרָֽח׃

passages.text: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
passages.sermon:
The east wind is strong and relentless.
The east wind acts with power.
The east wind claps its hands at the man.
The east wind hisses at the man.
The east wind drives the man out of his place.
passages.original: יִשְׂפֹּ֣ק עָלֵ֣ימוֹ כַפֵּ֑ימוֹ וְיִשְׁרֹ֥ק עָ֝לָ֗יו מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃
